A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoAM and CAIGen, with matching research objectives and experimental frameworks. Their text, tables, figures, equations and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite revisions and internal reporting inconsistencies in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation agreement and consistency analyses, MWE identification experiments, and fine-tuning and prompt-definition ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 reports revised original experiments and ablations, plus test-set type-tag auditing and continuity-based corpus and performance analyses.

M1.justification: The corpus type-tagging procedure changes from automatic tagging excluding UD to tagging all sources and manually correcting test-set types. Table 2 also adds AUX heads to the VERB category. The MaW and LLM identification procedures remain unchanged; the newly supplied pseudocode does not establish that every disclosed rule is new.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English MWE identification coverage from News, Commentary, TED and UD, and the same DiMSUM consistency-check sample. Discontinuous expressions already occur in v1; v2's continuity breakdown analyzes existing coverage. Newly discussed French data are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain the same four LLMs and MaW Rule, Rule+BiEnc and Rule+DCA systems. FT/FSL/ZSL, long/short-definition and input-output-format comparisons also retain their membership. The newly cited BERT tagging approach is proposed only for future evaluation.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 reports spaCy en_core_web_trf instead of en_core_web_lg, and Appendix B.1 changes Llama-70B's learning rate from 2e-4 to 1e-4. Type-based evaluation now uses manually corrected labels; maximum-pair agreement and continuity-stratified evaluation are added. The 780/521 sentence split, main metrics and most training settings remain unchanged. These disclosures do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused analyses of continuous versus discontinuous recall in Table 6b, discontinuity rates by type in Appendix A.4, and an additional failure case in Table 7. It also reports automatic type-tag errors and contextualizes annotation agreement. Existing seen/unseen, WordNet, fine-tuning, format and prompt-definition analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random training runs with means and standard deviations, and retain three-run reporting for FSL example selection and prompt-definition ablations. No changed run counts, significance tests, confidence intervals or uncertainty-estimation practices are documented; changed standard deviations are result updates.

E6.justification: Main results, subgroup recalls, corpus counts and both ablation tables are revised. Qwen-72B F1 changes from 55.5 to 57.8, while the reported Llama-8B long-versus-short-definition F1 gap contracts from 20.8 to 3.9 points. New Qwen-72B continuity recalls are 57.3 versus 17.1. Table 4's test-MWE count changes from 385 to 381. These substantially revise the empirical evidence; changed annotations and settings prevent interpreting them as clean same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The task formulation, exact-match precision/recall equations and idiomaticity versus compositionality reasoning are retained. Correcting the token subscript in Section 3 is a notation correction. The new tagging pseudocode supplies procedural detail without adding theoretical assumptions, proofs or guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract newly claims that CoAM is the first MWE identification dataset with MWE type tags. It also replaces the broad state-of-the-art comparison with the specific claim of outperforming MaW, which achieved state-of-the-art performance on DiMSUM; the conclusion drops the broader wording. The central dataset, interface and fine-tuning contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially reframes annotation reliability: the unchanged 37.3% agreement is defended through metric and cross-dataset comparisons, while v1's subjectivity explanation and corresponding limitations paragraph disappear. It adds dataset-size and method-coverage limitations, discusses residual training-type-tag errors, and emphasizes discontinuity as a remaining challenge. The forecast that a larger lexicon could substantially improve MaW is removed.

D1.justification: v1 promises public access upon acceptance; v2 states that CoAM and CAIGen are available and supplies dataset and source-code locations. Reproducibility documentation expands through tagging pseudocode, UD dependency-source information, interface-generation and nine-row details, and Appendix D instructions for restricted substitutions, reordered expressions and hyphens. Most existing hardware and runtime disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning definition modeling, idiomatic translation, Sequoia, PARSEME 1.1 agreement, discontinuous segmentation and BERT tagging. It removes Savary et al. (2019) and revises the rationale for excluding proper nouns using Navigli and Ponzetto (2012). These broaden the existing positioning without replacing its main research lineage.

P1.justification: v2 polishes wording throughout, expands the introduction and interface explanation, and reorganizes limitations into topical paragraphs. Annotation definitions and interface examples move from Appendix A into Appendix D, while the unseen-MWE definition moves into results analysis. The main section sequence and most exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Appendix presentation is substantially reorganized: A-C adopt two-column prose, while the relocated guidelines become an illustrated Appendix D. v2 adds Algorithm 1 and a continuity table, extends the results and case tables, and incorporates Figure 2's two retained examples into five inline illustrations. Table 1's columns are reordered and Figure 1's caption gains interface details.

improvement.justification: Manual correction of test-set type labels addresses a concrete weakness in v1's category-level evaluation. Continuity analysis, fuller guidelines and stated resource locations also improve diagnostic value and reuse. These gains are limited by inconsistent test counts (384 in Section 4.8 versus 381 in Table 4), stale claims of prompt-definition gains exceeding 12 points when Table 14 shows 3.9 and 11.4, and new pseudocode that can overwrite assigned types.
